scenes.say: Is filter coffee just an espresso with more water? No, and the reason is how the water moves.
The amount of water is not the difference, because the method is. Espresso is pushed through the coffee under pressure, while filter coffee drips through by gravity alone.

scenes.title: Pressure or gravity.
scenes.say: Espresso forces water through finely ground coffee, so you get a small, concentrated cup. Filter coffee lets water drip through coarser grounds, which gives a clear, light-bodied cup.

scenes.title: A long espresso is still espresso.
scenes.say: It gets more water, but that water is still pushed through fine coffee under pressure. Filter coffee skips the pressure, and a paper filter holds back some of the coffee's oils.

scenes.title: The tip.
scenes.say: If you want a filter-style cup at home, running your espresso longer will not get you there. You need a filter and a coarser grind.
So the difference is the method, not just more water. Send this to a friend who loves filter coffee.
